in men and pre-MP women the vCtDs and MIs are equally important for the BSI's and SSI's, while in post-MP the vCtDt is more influential than the MI.
, in healthy men and women, the BSI's are good indicators of bone strength, but their diagnostic value is not equal in different groups of individuals.

the BSI's are good indicators of mechanical competence in men and pre-MP women, and that the SSI is the most reliable index in post-MP females, but that the BSI values are not directly interpretable in terms of mechanical competence.

the vCtDs and the MIs are equally good indicators of mechanical competence, and that the BSIs, SSI, and their components, are useful diagnostic indicators of bone quality and design.

the BSI's are not a reliable indicator of the relative mechanical impact and diagnostic potential of the determinant factors, and that the diagnostic value of vCtDs and MIs should be evaluated separately.

the vCtDs are the most important determinant factor of the pQCT-assayed BSIs, but that their diagnostic value is limited by their relatively small variation, and that the diagnostic power of the indices depends on the variation of the MIs, which is larger, but varies naturally much more than that of the indices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vCtBMD should not be used to calculate BSIs in post-MP females.
the BSI's are not 'bone strength indices' in a mechanical sense.
the BSI's are not equally useful in all circumstances.
